title: Two superconducting pairing models with a Kitaev spin-liquid glue: microscopic kernel and parity alternation on odd-fold bond stars
abstract: We construct two superconducting pairing models on doped Kitaev honeycomb, whose microscopic kernels are derived rather than assumed. Both are driven by a bond-local glue neutral between the even- and odd-parity pairing channels; the chirality--parity linkage is set by bond-star geometry, not by the microscopic glue. (i) Model~1(odd-parity sector): the kernel follows from the flux-sector selection rule of the pure model, fixing its component-diagonal, nearest-neighbor separable, rank-one-per-bond form, with $w_α=J_K^2χ_α\propto r_αm_α$, where $m_α$ follows from the Hellmann--Feynman theorem and $r_α\simeq0.24$ is computed numerically. The spin-vertex state is a unitary triplet with a bond-locked anisotropic $\mathbf d$ vector; its gap is a Gram sum of bond sines, so nodal directions are fixed by geometry. (ii) Model~2(even): the kernel is fixed by the $C_3$ little-group selection rule of a zone-corner chiral phonon, up to a Cooper-channel extension whose momentum constraint we state explicitly. The charge-vertex pairing is a $d+id$ singlet: the parity decomposition $f_\pm=g_\pm+p_\pm$ projects onto $g_\pm$, so chirality is slaved to the phonon polarization, with $C=\pm4$ and $κ_{xy}/T=2κ_0$. Reversing the pump helicity reverses the Chern number, Kerr rotation, and thermal Hall sign. (iii) General theorem: on odd-fold bond stars, the angular-momentum ladder of a single-star chiral form factor alternates in parity. Every chiral state selected by such a bond-local form factor is a geometrically enforced singlet--triplet composite with universal amplitude ratios ($n=3$: $d\oplus p$; $n=5$: $g\oplus p$ or $d\oplus f$); coherent doubled-star combinations can restore parity purity. The Chern number of the mixed state follows the dominant on-shell component across a topological boundary. The spin glue drives $C=\pm2$; the charge kernel $C=\pm4$.
summary: This theoretical work develops two superconducting pairing models on the Kitaev honeycomb lattice by deriving the pairing kernels microscopically rather than assuming them. It establishes deep connections between lattice geometry, symmetry selection rules, and the resulting superconducting order parameter. The findings are crucial for understanding topological superconductivity in strongly correlated quantum magnets.
main_problem: The paper constructs and analyzes two superconducting pairing models derived microscopically on the doped Kitaev honeycomb lattice, focusing on how pairing symmetry is dictated by lattice geometry.
main_result: The models predict specific superconducting states (e.g., d+id singlet) whose topological properties, like the Chern number, are robustly linked to the lattice geometry and bond structure.
method: The analysis uses mean-field Bogoliubov-de Gennes theory, deriving pairing kernels from symmetry selection rules (flux-sector or $C_3$ little-group) and employing Majorana fermion techniques.
model_or_system: The system is superconducting pairing on the doped Kitaev honeycomb lattice, utilizing a bond-local glue mechanism. The theory involves mapping the spin-liquid ground state onto an effective electron-electron interaction.
key_observables: Superconducting gap ($\Delta$), Chern number ($C$), Thermal Hall Conductance ($\kappa_{xy}^T$), and the gap magnitude derived from bond sines.
important_parameters: Doping level, bond coupling strengths ($J_K$), and the geometry of the bond-star structure.
main_assumptions: The pairing glue is assumed to be bond-local and neutral between even- and odd-parity channels; the general theorem holds on odd-fold bond stars.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes mention tables detailing calculated values of the flux gap ($2\Delta_F$) and spectral weights.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the background (Kitaev model solution via Majorana fermions) to deriving two specific superconducting models (Model 1 for odd-parity, Model 2 for even-parity) and concluding with a general theorem regarding parity alternation on odd-fold bond stars.
why_interesting: The rigorous derivation of pairing symmetries from underlying lattice constraints (like bond-star geometry) provides a powerful, symmetry-enforced framework for understanding unconventional superconductivity in correlated materials.
